name: John son of Zebedee
role: Apostle, brother of James, a pillar of the Jerusalem church
whenBasis: From Jesus' ministry to Paul's meeting with the pillars in Jerusalem (Galatians 2:9), ≈AD 48–49. Tradition carries him to the end of the first century; see below.
summary: Son of Zebedee, brother of James, called from mending nets. With Peter and James he was in Jesus' inner circle. After the resurrection he went with Peter to the temple, where they healed a lame man and were arrested; the council marvelled at their boldness, seeing they were unschooled, ordinary men. He went with Peter to Samaria, and Paul names him with James and Cephas as a pillar of the Jerusalem church.
body: He tells Jesus they saw a man casting out demons in his name and tried to stop him. He and Peter prepare the Passover. The Gospel of John never names him; it speaks instead of the disciple whom Jesus loved.

moments.text: Stops a man casting out demons

later.text: Irenaeus (≈AD 180) says John, the Lord's disciple who leaned on his breast, wrote the Gospel at Ephesus and lived there into the reign of Trajan. Tradition also gives him the three letters and Revelation.
traditions: Catholic, Orthodox and Protestant readers who follow him

later.text: Raymond Brown, in his later work, held that the beloved disciple was not John son of Zebedee; Richard Bauckham argues for a different eyewitness, John the Elder.
